spot.html_text: Her criticisms of Descartes intertwine three distinct philosophical positions. First, she takes up the position of Aristotelian virtue ethics, in objecting that Descartes’s very liberal account of virtue, which requires only the intention to do good, does not require that one’s good intentions are realized in actions that are actually good. That is, she notes that Descartes makes virtue impervious to fortune or moral luck. She, however, goes beyond the canonical Aristotelian position to maintain
